newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Western Areas details hedge restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Western Areas details hedge restructuring.

text.p: South Africa's Western Areas Gold Mining Co Ltd on Friday released further details of the restructuring of its 1995 hedging transaction.

The firm said in a statement the restructuring was necessary to allow it to participate in increases in the rand gold price, while maintaining full protection against further weakening of the rand gold price to June 2001.
It also wanted to rearrange the funding component of the hedge to correspond more closely with the revised cash flow requirement of the company to June 2001.

The firm said the 1995 hedge had been replaced with a structure which involved the forward sale of 30 percent of planned production as well as the purchase of rand-gold put options for 70 percent of production for the period July 1997 to June 2001.

For the period July 2001 to June 2007, the company sold forward 20 percent of production in rand-gold and further sold rand-gold call options on 17.5 percent of production at forward rates and strike prices below the forward curve.

The only element of the 1995 hedge which remained was the deep out of the money dollar-rand call options that were bought to protect the mine against substantial depreciation in the rand from July 1997 to March 2004.
The net lower volume of gold committed to the new hedge required the purchase of 1.6 million ouces of gold to close out the excess volume of forward sales.

A cash payment of 75 million rand had been received in terms of this structured hedge which was adequate to cover the further cash shortfall which had accumulated since assessing a 60 million rand loan.
It said that operations would remain cash positive to June 2000 provided technical and economic assumptions were met.
The company added that it was withdrawing the cautionary announcement issued on July 23.
